tagline: Through the Dorchester marshes where Harriet Tubman's story begins.
intro: The byway leaves Cambridge, settled in 1684, and heads south into the marshes of Dorchester County, past the Tubman visitor center and through the Blackwater refuge, where the rivers run the color of tea from the peat. It passes near the Brodess Farm, where Harriet Tubman spent her younger years, and the store at Bucktown, then swings north through East New Market and Preston, with its Linchester gristmill, to Denton and Goldsboro.
Tubman went on to help more than 70 enslaved people escape. The route carries on through Delaware to Philadelphia, where she first found freedom.

moments.title: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: Marsh and forest largely unchanged since Tubman's time, now home to the East Coast's largest breeding population of bald eagles north of Florida.

moments.title: Bucktown
moments.text: At the village store, around 1835, the young Tubman tried to help an enslaved man avoid capture and was nearly killed for it.

moments.title: James Webb Cabin
moments.text: Built in 1852, the only log house left on the Eastern Shore from before the Civil War known to have been built by and for an African American.
